Compared to existing general segmentation algorithms, the proposed approach offers significant improvements in extraction accuracy. To foster further research, we release a point cloud dataset for LSAs extraction, which will be publicly available at: https://github.com/c175044/Line-Surge-Arresters-datasets .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A practical method for deriving all-weather ET from remote sensing and meteorological data
abstract: • A practical method based on machine-learning is proposed to calculate all-weather ET. • MODIS LST and Noah LST were combined and used as input for ET calculation. • An up-to-date ET product was generated based on the present method in Nebraska, USA. • RF has the best performance among the machine learning algorithms used in this study. Daily actual evapotranspiration (ET) is a crucial variable for efficient water resource management and irrigation planning, highlighting the need for timely and accurate ET products to support agricultural decision-making. This study presents a practical workflow for generating all-weather, daily ET data by integrating remote sensing and meteorological inputs. A pixel-wise land surface temperature (LST)–fractional vegetation cover (FVC) space is constructed based on energy balance theory, and a combination of remote sensing, meteorological, and physical model outputs are used as input features for machine learning (ML) algorithms to estimate ET. To address data gaps caused by cloud cover, land surface temperature (LST) derived from the Noah land surface model was utilized to supplement missing MODIS LST data, and separate ML models were developed for cloud-free and cloud-cover conditions. The ET predicted by both these models were integrated to produce all-weather ET. A comparative analysis between latent heat flux (LE) derived from this workflow and in-situ measurements collected in Nebraska (NE) during 2004 and 2012 demonstrated robust performance, R 2 and RMSE are 0.70 and 90.03 W/M 2 (NE1), 0.75 and 78.50 W/m 2 (NE2) and 0.75 and 79.77 W/m 2 (NE3), respectively. In the daily ET validation for 2020, R 2 and RMSEs are 0.76 and 0.96 mm, 0.75 and 1.04 mm, and 0.75 and 0.93 mm. Both profile and wall-to-wall comparisons demonstrate that the all-weather ET product effectively captures annual ET variability across the study region. The ET dataset is updated daily and is publicly accessible via CropSmart Data Information Portal.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A systematic review of social Media-Enabled flood disaster Informatics: Method, technology and application
abstract: Under the dual pressures of climate change and rapid urbanization, the frequent occurrence of flood disasters has become a global challenge. The widespread use of social media provides new perspectives for broader and more comprehensive perception of flood disaster events, and a social media-enabled flood disaster informatics framework has gradually taken shape. This study systematically reviews 607 publications from 2004 to 2024, aiming to reveal the research progress of utilizing social media big data in flood disaster management. By constructing a “method–technology–application” full-chain flood disaster informatics framework, this study highlights the flood information processing workflow featuring social media data, covering multiple aspects including social media data analysis, flood event detection, flood situation awareness, flood risk mapping, and emergency management practices. The literature review indicates that social media has been proven effective in compensating for the limitations of traditional flood monitoring approaches. In particular, multimodal data fusion and the application of artificial intelligence techniques can significantly enhance global flood monitoring capabilities. However, current research still faces challenges such as verifying data authenticity and integrating information across platforms. Future research should focus on exploring the transformative applications of foundation models (e.g., large language models, vision foundation models, and multimodal large models) with social media, including massive multi-source heterogeneous information understanding, generative disaster reporting and decision support, as well as real-time prediction and emergency simulation incorporating physical mechanisms. These advances are expected to drive a profound transformation of the intelligent emergency decision-making paradigm and provide a solid theoretical and technical foundation for the development of smart flood emergency management systems.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Shipborne bathymetry constrained denoising diffusion probabilistic model for seafloor DEM super-resolution
abstract: • We propose a bathymetry guided diffusion model (Bathy-DDPM) for seafloor modeling. • The Bathy-DDPM is used for seafloor DEM super-resolution reconstruction. • Shipborne bathymetric points guide seafloor terrain modeling via loss function. • Bathy-DDPM outperforms existing models and better retains terrain features. • Bathy-DDPM can be expanded globally for high-resolution data reconstruction. Seafloor topography is a fundamental element of the marine environment, playing a critical role in understanding geological evolution, hydrodynamic patterns, sediment distribution and benthic habitat structure. However, due to the low resolution of existing seafloor digital elevation models (DEMs), refined modelling techniques that can accurately represent the complexity of seafloor topographic environment are urgently needed. Aiming to address this need, this study introduces Bathy-DDPM, a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) that incorporates shipborne bathymetric data into its loss function to enhance DEM super-resolution. Leveraging GEBCO DEM data and single-beam bathymetric measurements, the model employs transfer learning by pretraining on land-based data and fine-tuning with limited marine datasets. Experimental results show that Bathy-DDPM consistently outperforms traditional interpolation methods and existing deep learning models (Bathy-CNN, Bathy-GAN, Bathy-TfaSR and Bathy-MSRResNet) across all the evaluation metrics. Compared to the advanced MSRResNet model, Bathy-DDPM achieves 18.2% reduction in MAE and a 15.2% reduction in RMSE, highlighting the efficacy of DDPM-based architectures in reconstructing complex seafloor topography. Additionally, Bathy-DDPM exhibits rapid convergence during training, improving training efficiency. The integration of shipborne bathymetric points also enhances performance across various deep learning models, particularly within GAN-based architectures. Furthermore, analysis results of bathymetry loss weight and measurement point density reveal that both factors notably influence model performance, with optimal results achieved at moderate loss weights and high spatial sampling densities. Overall, Bathy-DDPM shows strong potential for high-resolution seafloor reconstruction in data-scarce regions, offering valuable support for geospatial analysis and marine scientific research.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multiscale refined segment anything model based on multimodal remote sensing for surface feature recognition in open-pit mining areas
abstract: • A novel segment anything model-based framework for precise mining surface segmentation. • Multimodal fusion and multiscale refinement enhance SAM to tackle spectral and scale variations. • Adaptive fine-tuning incorporates mining knowledge, reducing computation and label requirements. Accurate land surface feature recognition is vital for geospatial analysis and Earth observation. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) excels in generalization, offering significant potential for remote sensing (RS) monitoring with limited annotated data. This study proposes MM-SAM, a SAM-based framework enhanced with multimodal and multiscale adaptations for fine-grained segmentation of heterogeneous surfaces in open-pit mining areas. Leveraging an adaptive fine-tuning strategy with minimal learnable parameters, MM-SAM tackles domain-specific challenges in mining environments via two key architectural innovations: 1) Multimodal RS Fusion (MRF), a preprocessing adapter integrates multispectral and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, extending SAM’s input from RGB to multidimensional spectral-spatial representations, effectively mitigating spectral distortions caused by terrain variations and cloud occlusions. 2) Multiscale Feature Enhancement (MFE), a lightweight multiscale convolutional adapter is embedded in the image encoder, coupled with a refinement branch in the decoder. This enables the integration of global semantic coherence with multiscale localized details, addressing significant scale variations in mining features. Experimental results demonstrate that MM-SAM achieves a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 69.99%, outperforming SAM by 17.88% and surpassing state-of-the-art methods. It also improves overall accuracy and macro F1 scores while showing robust temporal transferability, maintaining a consistent mIoU of 69.51% across datasets from different years. These confirm MM-SAM’s reliable performance and adaptability to open-pit mining landscapes, potentially advancing foundation models in complex geospatial tasks.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mitigating data Constraints in crop mapping: A self-supervised framework integrating adaptive clustering, graph convolution and global spatiotemporal attention
abstract: Correct classification of crop layers is crucial for crop growth tracking and estimating yields, but existing methods depends heavily on the completeness of data and ground truth labels. Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables crop mapping when data is limited. However, current SSL approaches fail to fully integrate information across spatiotemporal dimensions and lack the ability to learn and represent consistent ground object features. To this end, a self-supervised crop mapping framework is proposed, which integrates adaptive k-means clustering, graph convolution, and global spatiotemporal attention (SAKG). This framework reduces reliance on labeled data through contrastive learning and achieves implicit semantic grouping of crop spatiotemporal features using adaptive K-means clustering, graph convolution, and self-attention mechanisms, enhancing model robustness and representation of complex data while mitigating sample imbalance issues. Three experiments (cross spatial, cross temporal, cross Spatiotemporal) demonstrate that SAKG outperforms existing models in most transfer scenarios. Furthermore, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding(t-SNE) visualization verifies its effective reduction of spectral differences between the source and target domains, achieving consistent representation of crop features. Overall, this method can effectively utilize existing satellite data and labels to achieve large-scale crop mapping. The code can be obtained here: https://github.com/LijianXie/SAKG-net .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GeoKG-HSA: A framework for habitat suitability assessment with geospatial knowledge graphs
abstract: • Proposes a novel framework for habitat suitability assessment. • Links species and environmental factors via geospatial knowledge graphs. • Demonstrates improved performance over traditional models in a real case study. Habitat suitability, which reflects how well environmental conditions support species survival, growth, and reproduction, is highly sensitive to climate change and human activities and underpins effective conservation policy-making. Traditional machine learning models for habitat suitability assessment often struggle to capture complex semantic relationships among environmental factors and suffer from limited spatial generalization. To overcome these limitations, we propose GeoKG-HSA, a novel framework leveraging geospatial knowledge graphs to enhance habitat suitability assessment. By adopting an ontology-based approach, GeoKG-HSA explicitly models semantic relationships among diverse environmental variables, enabling structured integration of multi-source heterogeneous habitat data. The framework further integrates symbolic domain knowledge with data-driven machine learning, establishing a hybrid paradigm that improves both interpretability and predictive accuracy. A case study on Tundra Swan habitat in a wetland ecosystem shows that, on average across four models, GeoKG-HSA improves precision by 0.147, recall by 0.281, and F1 score by 0.255. Area Under the Curve (AUC) scores were also improved by 0.04 for the logistic regression model, 0.20 for the support vector machine model, 0.06 for the decision tree model, and 0.13 for the multi-layer perceptron model. Compared with the MaxEnt, GeoKG-HSA exhibits superior spatial generalization in regions with missing or sparse samples. These results demonstrate that GeoKG-HSA effectively integrates multi-source environmental data, enhances model generalizability, and significantly outperforms traditional Tabular-HSA methods. This framework offers a promising tool for advancing biodiversity conservation and ecosystem management under changing environmental conditions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Corrigendum to “A framework for road space extraction from point clouds and integration into 3D city models.” [Int. J. Appl. Earth Obs. Geoinf. 143 (2025) 104803]
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Bayesian Network analysis of spatial disparities in child nutrition status and health determinants across Indonesia
abstract: • The research employs Bayesian Network and spatial analysis to pinpoint critical factors contributing to child malnutrition in Indonesia. • Exclusive breastfeeding, immunization, antenatal care, and growth monitoring are essential determinants affecting nutritional outcomes. • High-risk groups of malnutrition are found, which shows where targeted interventions are needed. • The model evaluation demonstrates robust predictive performance for various variables, although certain indicators necessitate supplementary contextual data. • Findings support evidence-based policies that are in line with Indonesia’s National Strategy for Stunting Reduction to improve the nutrition of children all over the country. Child malnutrition continues to be a significant public health issue in Indonesia, with considerable spatial variations among provinces. This study utilizes an integrated framework that combines Bayesian Network (BN) modeling, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Moran’s I analysis to ascertain the principal determinants of child nutritional status and their spatial distribution. The Bayesian Network (BN) probabilistic approach captures intricate interdependencies among health and behavioral factors, such as Correct Knowledge about Stunting (CKS), Exclusive Breastfeeding (EBF), Breastfeeding for Two Years (BF2Y), Complementary Feeding (CF), Immunization (IMM), Growth Monitoring (GM), Iron-Folic Acid Supplementation (IFA), Antenatal Care (ANC6), and Animal Protein Intake for Pregnant Women (APH), and their impact on outcomes classified as Severely Underweight (SUW), Underweight (UW), and Normal (N). Spatial statistical analyses indicate considerable heterogeneity and elevated-risk clusters of malnutrition, underscoring areas necessitating prioritized interventions. Stochastic simulations elucidate the variability and robustness of critical determinants, whereas model evaluation via Mean Squared Error (MSE) indicates robust predictive performance for variables such as N, ANC6, and SUW, with heightened uncertainty noted for EBF, IFA, and IMM, implying the impact of supplementary social or contextual factors. This study combines probabilistic inference with spatial analysis to show the pathways and interactions that lead to child malnutrition. This gives useful information for focused, evidence-based interventions. The results support strategies that involve more than one sector and are in line with Indonesia’s National Strategy for Stunting Reduction (Presidential Regulation No. 72 of 2021). This will help resources be used more effectively, policies be planned better, and children’s nutrition outcomes be more fair across the country.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: UAV-based remote sensing estimation of above-ground biomass in different crops: A review
abstract: Above-ground biomass (AGB) is a measure used to assess crop growth and estimate yield. Accurate, non-destructive and rapid AGB estimation is crucial for advancing modern agriculture. Unlike traditional destructive survey methods, the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides a highly flexible and low-cost way. This study provides a systematic review in terms of UAV-based AGB estimation, including the UAV monitoring mechanisms, UAV platforms, sensors, features, methods, and difficulties and future development directions in AGB estimation. Also, this study subjectively evaluates functions and limitations of different sensors, features, estimation methods, and explores the application and prospects for the development of crop AGB estimation models. Given the current challenges of UAV-based AGB estimation, some important directions for future research are also provided. This review aims to provide practical strategies for future research on estimating AGB and enhancing the efficiency of this technique in assessing crop growth and yield prediction, thereby promoting the development of precision agriculture.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Prior information guided cost optimization for terrain generation from high-resolution orbiter imagery of lunar south pole
abstract: Precise reconstruction of lunar south pole’s terrain is crucial for future exploration missions, particularly for landing site selection, resource identification, and scientific research. However, the challenging illumination conditions, characterized by extensive shadowed areas, pose significant challenges to traditional photogrammetric methods. The shadowed areas lead to poor disparity estimation and less accurate terrain models, highlighting the need for improved techniques that can effectively address these difficult conditions. This study proposes an enhanced dense matching method for terrain reconstruction at lunar south pole, which incorporates prior information of existing lower-resolution terrain model to guide the semi-global matching (SGM) process. We begin by adaptively selecting seed points in shadowed areas of the image through intensity histogram analysis. Homogeneous pixels with close spatial distance and small intensity difference surrounding each seed point are then identified based on distance and intensity differences. After obtaining prior disparity values, the corresponding costs are simulated and combined with matching costs from the original 2D disparity search SGM algorithm, optimizing pixel costs to refine the cost volume and improve the robustness of the matching process. Experiments were conducted in representative areas of lunar south pole to validate the effectiveness of our method. Additionally, the performance of our method is compared with SGM variants and two advanced cost volume optimization methods, further demonstrating its effectiveness. Finally, we apply our method to several pairs of LROC NAC images to generate detailed terrain models at lunar south pole, quantitatively validating its reliability through comparisons with reference terrain data and LOLA laser points. • Enhance matching robustness in shadowed areas using prior information. • Select seed points adaptively in difficult areas to overcome random sampling limits. • Improve photogrammetric terrain mapping performance at lunar south pole.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Assessing four-decade spatiotemporal changes of chlorophyll-a concentration in lakes and reservoirs of the mid-lower yangtze river basin using landsat imagery and machine learning
abstract: • A machine learning based approach was developed to estimate Chla from Landsat data. • Chla variations in Mid-Lower Yangtze River Basin were observed over four decades. • Chla showed an rose and then fell interannual trend with a turning point in 2005–2007. • Precipitation and temperature were key factors affecting Chla spatial distribution. • Nighttime light intensity was negatively correlated to Chla interannual variation. Eutrophication has become a persistent environmental challenge in the Mid-Lower Yangtze River Basin (MLYRB), influencing both water security and regional sustainability. Remote sensing provides an effective approach for retrieving chlorophyll-a concentrations (Chla). However, due to the limited spatial and temporal coverage of satellite observations and inconsistencies among satellite sensors, long-term variations in Chla across the MLYRB have not been thoroughly investigated. This study aims to fill this gap by generating a four-decade (1984–2024) Chla dataset for lakes and reservoirs larger than 1 km 2 in the MLYRB using Landsat imagery. In this study, Landsat-5 TM and Landsat-8 OLI imagery were used to develop a machine learning approach based on the gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) to estimate Chla, calibrated with 235 synchronized satellite and in situ measurements. The model showed strong performance on the testing dataset ( R 2 = 0.78, RMSLE = 0.21, AURE = 29.6 %) and was subsequently applied to reconstruct annual Chla maps for lakes and reservoirs across the MLYRB from 1984 to 2024. The reconstructed results revealed that Chla were highest in the Dongting Lake and Poyang Lake sub-basins (27.9 ± 2.5 and 27.8 ± 2.7 mg/m 3 , respectively) and lowest in the Han River and Taihu Lake sub-basins (22.7 ± 2.5 and 22.8 ± 2.1 mg/m 3 ). Spatially, Chla distribution was strongly correlated with precipitation and temperature, which together accounted for 72.4 % of the spatial variability. A distinct transition occurred between 2005 and 2007, when mean Chla peaked at 27.6 ± 8.5 mg/m 3 and the overall trend shifted from fluctuating increases to a decline. Temporally, Chla variations were largely associated with, meteorological factors, particularly nighttime light (NTL) and gross domestic product (GDP), explaining 65 % of the temporal variability. This study presents the first nearly four-decade Landsat-derived Chla dataset for lakes and reservoirs larger than 1 km 2 in the MLYRB. This long-term dataset offers critical support for understanding water quality dynamics and guiding evidence-based environmental management in eastern plains of China.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Storm response of the upper intertidal zone on a gravel beach
abstract: • In a 42-year hindcast context: 2019–2020 can be considered an exceptionally energetic winter season; 2018–2019 moderate. • Video monitoring quantified upper-intertidal volume and shoreline changes. • Storm impact controlled by storm characteristics, tide range during storm impact, and previous beach morphology conditions. • Multiple regression (wave height + tide range during storm impact) explains 46 % of volume change related to storm event. • Storm clusters often erode but can also promote recovery during lower-energy phases. This paper investigates morphodynamics of a macrotidal gravel beach (Etretat, Normandy, NW France) during two consecutive winter seasons characterized by moderate (2018–2019) and exceptionally energetic (2019–2020) conditions according to a 42-year analysis of hindcasted wave data. Upper intertidal beach changes and shoreline data were derived from a video monitoring system. The results show that storm impacts were strongly influenced by the storm characteristics, the tide phasing, and more importantly, by the pre-existing conditions of the beach before the impact of the storms. A multiple regression including wave height and tide range during the storm event explained 46% of the variance of the volume change due to storm events. Storm clusters often cause beach erosion but can also contribute significantly to beach recovery.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatially generalizable bias correction of satellite solar radiation for regional climate assessment—a case study in Japan
abstract: • Evaluation of Himawari-8 surface solar radiation (SSR) using ground observations. • Bias correction of Himawari SSR via an interpretable ensemble learner. • Assessment of the spatial transferability of the correction. • Evaluation of high-resolution regional reanalysis by bias-corrected satellite SSR. Evaluations of model- and reanalysis-based surface solar radiation (SSR) products often depend on satellite-derived estimates, which can be biased, particularly under broken-cloud conditions or over high-albedo surfaces. In this study, we first evaluated JAXA’s Himawari satellite SSR against ground-based observations. We then combined sparse but accurate ground measurements with high-resolution meteorological data to train an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model that captures and spatiotemporally extrapolates the systematic bias between satellite SSR and ground truth data. Our model is physics-informed, interpretable via feature-attribution analyses, and generalizes across snow-covered terrain. Applying this correction over Japan, we achieved close spatial pattern alignment with a distinct ground-based gridded SSR dataset, which further allowed us to examine the spatial transferability of the correction method. Finally, we used the bias-corrected satellite SSR data to assess a novel high-resolution regional reanalysis, and found that the reanalysis data reproduce expected spatial patterns and overall SSR magnitudes well but tend to slightly overestimate the SSR data under cloudy skies. However, especially under clear skies, the reanalysis remains valuable for refining bias-corrected satellite SSR data in certain high-altitude mountainous regions, where our machine learning model struggles to extrapolate. Overall, the proposed method shows promise for application across platforms and regions, enabling more reliable datasets for climate assessment and downscaling.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Trends and drivers of Arctic lake color change from Landsat time series
abstract: • Declining red and green surface reflectance in western Canadian Arctic lakes. • Abrupt changes in lake color and NDTI associated with slumping and wildfire. • Lake color change follows warm summer temperature with a 2-year lag. • Tailored cross-sensor calibration of Landsat essential for Arctic lake studies. Arctic lake color and quality are changing in response to the warming climate, permafrost degradation, and intensifying disturbances. These changes have important implications on carbon and nutrient cycling, wildlife habitat, and water resources planning. However, the drivers, spatial distribution, and long-term trajectories of these changes remain poorly characterized on regional scales (∼100 km). In this study, we examined over 3,000 lakes in part of the Mackenzie Delta, Tuktoyaktuk Coastlands, and adjacent upland tundra in the Northwest Territories, Canada, to quantify both gradual and abrupt changes in lake color using harmonized Landsat time series from 1985 to 2022. Across the region, we found average declines of surface reflectance in the red and green bands by 13 % and 15 % over the last four decades, respectively. In comparison, the Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) trends differed between sub-regions, with a decadal increase in the Tuktoyaktuk Coastlands and a decrease in the Mackenzie Delta. We identified a positive, lagged correlation between abrupt lake color change and mean summer air temperature (MSAT), particularly in the Tuktoyaktuk Coastlands (R = 0.7, lag = 2 years), indicating a delayed impact of warm summers on lake color. One important mechanism of such impact was lakeshore thaw slumping intensified by rising summer temperatures, with slump-affected lakes experiencing abrupt increases in surface reflectance and NDTI driven by sediment input. We identified fire as another important driver of lake color dynamics, which led to greater changes in lake surface reflectance (p < 0.01) and NDTI (p = 0.1) compared to surrounding lakes. These findings demonstrate the value of harmonized Landsat time series for characterizing multifaceted Arctic lake color dynamics, along with their drivers and impacts.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Nationwide spatial distribution of aquaculture ponds in China: Inland surpassing coastal areas revealed by Satellite remote sensing
abstract: • A novel OS-APM workflow was developed to map aquaculture ponds (APs). • First national-scale annual 10-m AP datasets (2016–2023) in China were made. • Inland dominated China’s contemporary aquaculture landscape (56% vs. coastal 44%) • AP area exhibited an inverted-U trend (peak 2019) with 14% contraction by 2023. • The reversal was strongly correlated with China’s ecological civilization initiatives. Rapid expansion of China’s aquaculture ponds (APs) has significantly contributed to food security and economic development, yet simultaneously triggering ecological degradation. However, the absence of high-resolution national datasets has constrained systematic analyses of APs’ spatiotemporal dynamics and their transboundary environmental footprints. To fill this gap, we developed a robust approach for accurately monitoring APs across China and elucidating the spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying mechanisms driving their changes. The Optical-SAR Aquaculture Pond Mapper (OS-APM) was developed, a novel framework integrating spatiotemporal-spectral signatures to synergistically leverage multi-sensor time series for precision AP mapping. The OS-APM comprised a hierarchical segmentation strategy for large-scale AP delineation, multi-modal feature fusion to distinguish spectrally ambiguous classes, and an ensemble classifier integrating optical, SAR, geometric, and topographic features. The framework achieved individual-pond-scale extraction accuracy (OA > 90 %) and generated China’s first 10-m resolution annual AP dataset (China_AP), derived from 119,882 Sentinel-1 and 579,436 Sentinel-2 scenes (2016–2023). This dataset revealed previously undocumented spatiotemporal patterns, indicating a 2023 AP inventory of 19,919.52 km 2 , with inland systems (55.56 %) now surpassing coastal ones (44.44 %) to dominate China’s aquaculture landscape. Spatially, four provinces (Jiangsu, Hubei, Shandong, Guangdong) collectively host 56 % of national APs, with 58 % clustered in the Yangtze-Huaihe River corridors. Temporally, the AP area exhibited an inverted-U trajectory, increasing from 20,685.20 km 2 (2016) to a peak of 23,256.84 km 2 (2019), then contracting below initial levels to 19,919.52 km 2 by 2023. This reversal strongly correlates with China’s ecological civilization initiatives, notably the 2017 Aquaculture Water and Tidal Flat Plan. This study establishes multi-sensor data for national AP monitoring, quantifies inland AP expansion patterns under policy regulation, and delivers a scientific foundation for reconciling aquaculture intensification with wetland conservation.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of wildfire severity in California, United States via satellite imagery and in-situ data, 2000–2023
abstract: • Spatiotemporal wildfire assessment (2000–2023) integrating satellite and in-situ data. • Advanced CEEMD + TDIC reveal nonlinear wildfire–climate dynamics across timescales. • Novel IDF curves quantify wildfire intensity–duration–frequency characteristics. • Regional divergence: severity rising statewide despite declining occurrence in some zones. • Temperature & VPD amplify, while soil moisture & rainfall suppress, wildfire activity. California experiences hundreds of wildfires each year, posing increasing risks to ecosystems and communities. This study investigates how hydrometeorological drivers influence wildfire occurrence and severity across four ecological zones from 2000 to 2023, using satellite imagery and in situ data. Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD), Pseudo–Tri-Dimensional CEEMD, and Time-Dependent Intrinsic Correlation (TDIC) were applied to decompose short- and long-term variability, and Intensity–Duration–Frequency (IDF) curves were utilized to characterize event intensity and duration. Results show that wildfire severity has increased statewide even as occurrence rates diverged regionally. In the Sierra, the number of fires declined by approximately 25 %, yet the average daily burned area doubled, indicating fewer but more destructive events. In the North Coast, fire frequency decreased after 2010, but severity continued to rise, while the Central and South Coasts experienced more frequent ignitions that peaked around 2018. TDIC-based analysis revealed that wildfire occurrence decreases sharply with higher precipitation (≈ −0.7) and soil moisture (≈ −0.8), while hot and dry conditions strongly amplify fire activity, with temperature (≈ +0.8) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD; ≈ +0.6) emerging as dominant drivers. Vegetation greenness, measured by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), exerted contrasting effects: in the Sierra, dense summer biomass fueled larger fires once dried (+0.7), whereas in the South Coast, senescent grasses supported more ignitions (−0.8). IDF analysis further demonstrated that two- to five-day events often reached daily intensities exceeding 500,000 ha, while longer events accumulated greater total burned areas despite lower daily rates. These findings provide quantitative evidence that wildfire–climate interactions in California are region-specific and increasingly shaped by hotter, drier conditions, underscoring the need for adaptive fire management tailored to both short-term extremes and long-term fuel dynamics.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-modal cross Swin transformer network for multi-label classification landslide detection with optical and SAR images of Luding
abstract: Natural phenomena such as earthquakes and heavy rainfall can trigger landslide events hundreds or even thousands of times in a given area. Therefore, rapid and efficient intervention in affected regions is essential. Existing studies have demonstrated good detection performance using optical remote sensing images; however, optical data has significant limitations under cloud cover. Moreover, current multi-modal fusion methods struggle to effectively capture the nonlinear interactions between different modes when processing data with large informational disparities. To address these issues, we developed the China Luding multi-modal landslide dataset, which includes optical and polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) images. We also propose a multi-modal network for landslide detection based on multi-label classification, called multi-modal cross Swin Transformer network (MCSTNet). Additionally, a new weighted asymmetric loss function (WASL) is proposed to improve multi-label classification tasks. Our proposed network consists of two stages: feature extraction and feature fusion. In the first stage, two independent branches extract high-level semantic features from optical and PolSAR images. In the second stage, a multi-modal cross multi-head self-attention (MCMSA) mechanism fuses the high-level semantic features from the multi-modal information. Therefore, the model enhances the learning and feature representation capabilities through parallel processing the input data information in different representation subspaces. Compared to other recent landslide detection methods, our results indicate that the proposed method is more effective, achieving an F 1 score of 88.24% for landslide detection, with greater accuracy in identifying landslide-prone areas. Therefore, our model can provide reliable and effective decision support for disaster emergency responses.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: HRCM: Human–Robot LiDAR-inertial collaborative mapping with robust triangulated planes
abstract: Multirobot Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has become a hot spot all over the world while there still exist some key issues to be addressed for collaborative mapping, especially for heterogenous platforms. This paper presents a self-designed LiDAR-inertial-mapping system on lightweight manned helmet and unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) platforms. A stable-triangular-descriptor-based place recognition method is proposed to detect overlap between varied field of view (FoV), followed by a Delaunay verification to restrain the global similarity. Based on the conjugated plane primitives across the platforms, bundle adjustment is derived to enhance the map consistency. All frames within the sliding window will be mutually constrained and optimized through the collective pose graph. Experiments on place recognition, pose estimation and point cloud mapping are conducted in different kinds of environments. Compared to other famous works (e.g. FastLIO2, LIOSAM, PointLIO), our system can attain the best results in almost all cases. The final improvements against them of mapping precision reach 15.71% with same LiDAR and 14.49% for heterogenous LiDARs on UGV. As for the helmet, this disparity varies from 0.6% for dataset with small intersection to 22.33% at most.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A global long-term (2002–2022) C-band vegetation optical depth record retrieved after merging AMSR-E, AMSR2 and WindSat
abstract: • Proposed a calibration method for merging TB observations from three sensors. • Assessed the long-term C-VOD retrieved from the merged TB. • The long-term C-VOD was found to be highly consistent over three sensors. Vegetation optical depth (VOD) based on microwave remote sensing has become an essential indicator for monitoring large-scale vegetation conditions. The relatively long-term record of satellite-based passive C-band observations offers the potential for assessing dynamic vegetation changes. Due to the limited operational lifetime of individual microwave sensors, retrieving a long-term C-band VOD (C-VOD) dataset often requires combining multiple sensors, such as Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer for EOS Aqua (AMSR-E, 2002–2011), Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2, 2012–present) and WindSat (2003–2020). Retrieving a long-term C-VOD from their C-band brightness temperature (TB) observations faces two major challenges: (i) non-negligible systematic biases exist between the TB observations among the three sensors; (ii) TB from different sensors may not be strongly associated, especially in tropical forests with small seasonal variations. To address these challenges, we employed a combined inter-calibration method, using linear regression in sparse vegetation and linear rescaling in dense vegetation, to merge TB from three sensors. Results showed that: (i) in undisturbed dense forests where minimal emissivity variation can be assumed, the merged TB (2002–2022) exhibited strong temporal correlations with skin temperature (H polarization: R = 0.90, V polarization: R = 0.86); (ii) the merged C-VOD retrieved from the merged TB exhibited substantially improved temporal consistency across three sensors, reducing global discrepancies between AMSR-E and AMSR2 from 6.20 % to 0.34 %. Furthermore, the merged C-VOD showed stable long-term consistency across sensors, with paired t-tests indicating no significant differences (P-value > 0.01) at the global and vegetation-type scales, confirming reliable cross-sensor continuity; (iii) the merged C-VOD showed stronger temporal correlations with normalized difference vegetation index, enhanced vegetation index, and site-level gross primary production across more vegetated areas globally, and exhibited higher and more stable spatial correlations with vegetation variables across sensor transitions compared to the existing merged C-VOD product.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An improved ROBust OpTimization-based (iROBOT) fusion model for reliable spatiotemporal seamless remote sensing data reconstruction
abstract: • iROBOT is proposed as an improved version of the ROBOT fusion model for spatiotemporal reconstruction. • It replaces fixed rectangular blocks with spectrally and spatially homogeneous segments to suppress block artifacts. • An adaptive gap-filling strategy, coupled with low-quality information detection, is introduced to improve robustness under cloud-affected conditions. • Experiments across two representative areas show consistent improvements over ROBOT, OL-HSTFM, and FSDAF. • It achieves higher accuracy while maintaining efficiency, supporting reliable seamless data cube reconstruction at global scales. Spatiotemporal fusion is recognized as a feasible approach for reconstructing high spatiotemporal resolution remote sensing imagery. The recently proposed ROBust OpTimization-based (ROBOT) fusion model has attracted attention for its efficiency, accuracy, and simple parameterization, and has been applied to seamless global data cube reconstruction. However, its sliding-window strategy often leads to block artifacts, while cloud contamination in auxiliary images further degrade the reconstruction quality and reliability. To address these limitations, this study proposes an improved version of ROBOT (iROBOT). By replacing fixed rectangular patches with spectrally and spatially homogeneous segments, iROBOT effectively suppresses block artifacts and better preserves structural details. In addition, an adaptive gap-filling strategy is applied to temporally nearest auxiliary images prior to fusion, and a low-quality information detection module is introduced to filter unreliable cloud-contaminated data from the regression and residual allocation steps, thereby enhancing reliability under cloud contamination. A total of 28 experiments conducted across two representative areas demonstrate that iROBOT consistently outperforms ROBOT, OL-HSTFM, and FSDAF under both cloud-free and cloud-contaminated scenarios. Moreover, compared with ROBOT, iROBOT exhibits superior capability in selecting reliable information from multi-temporal auxiliary images, with its accuracy advantage becoming more pronounced as the number of auxiliary inputs increases, and with notably enhanced robustness in cloud-prone environments. These findings highlight the potential of iROBOT for improving the accuracy of global-scale spatiotemporal image reconstruction. Code is found at https://github.com/Andy-cumt/iROBOT_spatiotemporal-fusion .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Evaluating the impact of canopy spatial heterogeneity on Solar-Induced chlorophyll fluorescence and Model-Based quantification
abstract: Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) is a powerful proxy for vegetation photosynthesis. However, its broader application remains constrained by the insufficient understanding and quantification of canopy spatial heterogeneity. We used the 3D discrete anisotropic radiative transfer (DART) model to simulate SIF. Heterogeneous and homogeneous canopies were compared to quantify the impact of canopy spatial configuration on total leaf-emitted SIF (SIF total ) and hemispherically integrated top-of-canopy SIF (SIF hemi ). Angular effects were examined by comparing top-of-canopy SIF (SIF toc ) with SIF total estimated at different viewing angles. We also compared the relationships of simulated SIF total and SIF toc with fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation ( f APAR) and vegetation indices (VIs). In addition, we evaluated the relationships between the coefficient of variation (CV) of VIs and SIF, and developed a correction function for estimating heterogeneous-canopy SIF using homogeneous-canopy SIF. The results reveal that (1) both SIF total and SIF hemi are significantly higher in homogeneous than in heterogeneous canopies; (2) estimating SIF total from SIF toc effectively reduces angular dependency; (3) SIF total exhibits the strongest correlation with f APAR, while SIF toc aligns better with NIRv and EVI; and (4) VI-derived CVs are negatively correlated with SIF, with CV NIRv and CV EVI at 10 m resolution demonstrating robust performance in fitting the ratio of heterogeneous-to-homogeneous canopy SIF, validating the proposed correction function. This study highlights the critical role of canopy structural heterogeneity in shaping SIF and presents an approach to convert homogeneous-canopy SIF to heterogeneous-canopy conditions, offering a novel pathway toward more accurate SIF estimation and application.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mapping forest landscape fragmentations under different fire severity using Sentinel-2 data with SNIC-MVI RF
abstract: • SNIC-MVI RF can accurately get forest landscape fragmentation in mountain areas. • Indices segmented from pixels to objects can relieve “salt and pepper” noises. • Significant differences exist in post-fire forest landscape fragmentation indices. • Pre-fire meteorological conditions and vegetation coverage are two main factors. Mapping forest landscape fragmentation (FLF) after fires is essential for maintaining ecosystem balance, reducing fire-related losses, and minimizing environmental damage. However, the “salt-and-pepper” phenomenon complicates accurate FLF mapping at fine resolutions (≤ 10 m) in mountainous regions. To relieve the phenomenon, this study used the multi-vegetation index (MVI) to represent FLF and applied the Simple Non-Iterative Clustering (SNIC) algorithm to convert pixels into objects before classification, and then SNIC-MVI RF was introduced to map FLF using Sentinel-2 imagery and land use data. In combination with topographical and meteorological data, the Geodetector was employed to analyze the influencing factors on FLF patterns across different fire severity ranges. The results indicate that: (1) The proposed SNIC-MVI RF can accurately retrieve FLF across a range of fire severity using 10-m Sentinel-2 imagery while mitigating the “salt-and-pepper” phenomenon, with an average precision of 96.2 % and an average F1-score of 97.4 %. (2) The FLF spatial patterns exhibit significant differences across fire severity. Low fire severity (LFS) leads to an increase in the number of small patches, moderate fire severity (MFS) results in more complex patch edges, and high fire severity (HFS) promotes greater patch aggregation. (3) Pre-fire meteorological conditions and vegetation cover are major influences on the spatial patterns of FLF under different fire severities. This study will provide a new method for exploring the impact of different fire severities on FLF in central Yunnan. As an important indicator for assessing ecological disturbance and habitat degradation, analyzing the response of fragmentation to different fire severities can help administrators evaluate the impacts of fire on FLF more scientifically and develop more targeted and sustainable forest management and ecological restoration strategies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Land surface change detection after major volcanic eruptions in Indonesia using Machine learning and Spatial-Temporal transferability
abstract: • Historical eruption data enhances model accuracy in data-scarce environments; • Integration of SAR and optical data enhances volcanic deposit mapping; • Random Forest and XGBoost consistently outperform SVM for volcanic impact mapping. Mitigating volcanic eruption disasters is a key priority in Indonesia’s national development agenda. Due to the high density of active volcanoes near populated areas, even eruptions with a relatively low Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) can result in significant fatalities and losses. Therefore, rapid mapping of eruption impacts is essential both during and following an eruption. Machine learning with Earth Observation (EO) data enhances the speed and accuracy of volcanic impact mapping, critical for timely disaster response. In this study, we evaluate the performance of three machine learning classifiers − Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost – for mapping land surface changes resulting from volcanic deposits (e.g. lahars, pyroclastic density currents and lava) across three different data availability scenarios using multi-temporal Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 optical data. Scenario I use a traditional approach, where training and validation data are sourced from the same eruption event. In Scenario II , the spatial transfer scenario, we simulate the absence of local training data by using data from different volcanoes. In Scenario III , the spatial–temporal transfer scenario, we include training data from past eruptions of the target volcano in addition to other events. Our results demonstrate that Scenario I achieve the highest classification accuracy, with Random Forest and XGBoost consistently outperforming SVM, achieving f1-scores exceeding 0.90. Scenario III improves average model performance compared to Scenario II (Δf1-score – 0.12), highlighting the value of historical eruption data for enhancing classification accuracy in data-scarce environments. These findings underscore the critical role of integrating EO data and machine learning in advancing volcanic impact mapping, offering a scalable and efficient approach to support disaster management efforts globally.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: 3D surface displacement modeling in Lorca, Spain, using dual-orbit MT-InSAR and multiple prior constraints
abstract: • Horizontal displacement in Lorca reveals alignment with the AMF strike. • 3D deformation shows that the left tectonic activity is dormant in Lorca (2015–2017). • 3D surface deformation monitoring via MT-InSAR and multiple prior models. Excessive groundwater pumping is a significant driver of land deformation, potentially threatening regional geological stability. Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) has been widely used to monitor such deformation. However, existing studies primarily focus on retrieving InSAR line-of-sight (LOS) or ground vertical deformation, limiting insights into three-dimensional (3D) ground displacements driven by subsurface processes. To address this, we propose a novel approach for modeling 3D surface displacement by integrating dual-orbit Multi-Temporal InSAR measurements with multiple prior deformation models. Specifically, we first estimate two sets of 3D displacements using a Bayesian approach by integrating dual-orbit InSAR measurements into prior models. Subsequently, bidirectional matching is employed to identify reliable homologous points, which are then used to reconstruct the complete horizontal displacement fields through the surface horizontal force equilibrium equation. Following the proposed methodology, for multi-track and high-coherence data, minimum acceleration (MinA) combination, multiple-aperture interferometry (MAI), and burst-overlap interferometry (BOI) techniques can serve as alternatives to conventional approaches. Moreover, incorporating along-track motion will further enhance 3D deformation estimation using SAR data. In the Lorca basin, Spain, we utilized Sentinel-1A ascending and descending SAR images to construct high-precision 3D cumulative displacement fields between October 7, 2015, to March 24, 2017. The experimental results reveal a maximum cumulative subsidence of 121.5 mm and notable horizontal displacements with a peak magnitude of 18.6 mm, a component that has received limited attention in earlier studies. The proposed approach eliminates the need for ground-based observations and yields improvements of 33.7 %, 51.3 %, and 43.9 % in the accuracy of vertical, east–west, and north–south deformation components, respectively, compared to the SMVCE method that integrates both InSAR and GNSS data. This study addresses the low sensitivity of InSAR in monitoring north–south displacement induced by groundwater extraction, offering new evidence to elucidate deformation mechanisms and providing valuable implications for sustainable groundwater management and geohazard mitigation.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Take a photo of the river! Assessing the feasibility of using Google Street View images as source materials for assessing river hydromorphology
abstract: The development of documentation technologies in the science of aquatic ecosystems provides a lot of new data. Some sets of documentary data, although developed for a different purpose, can be used to increase the effectiveness of water management and better protection of riverscapes.. Such a source of data is riverscape photos available in geolocation services, based on which it is possible to assess the state of the river environment. In our article, we attempted to assess the hydromorphological condition of rivers based on available riverscape photos in Google Street View (GSV). In accordance with the River Habitat Survey protocol - one of the classic methods of assessing the hydromorphological condition implemented worldwide, we assessed the parameters of the hydromorphological condition of 60 stretches of selected Polish rivers located in different regions of the country, having specific and different physiographic features (slope, flow velocity, discharge, modification). Then, based on available multimedia materials (GSV photos), we independently assessed the same parameters affecting the class of the hydromorphological condition of rivers and performed a comparative statistical analysis. In our comparative study we revealed that there is no statistically significant difference between the assessment of the hydromorphological river status using the standard RHS field protocol and the assessment using GSV (p values of the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test 0.19 – 0.98). Although the results require further verification on larger data sets, we see significant potential for using GSV in supplementing field methods of river hydromorphology assessment with this data. We postulate that in the absence of field analyses and with the availability of GSV materials or other photographic materials from rivers (e.g. citizen science), a reliable assessment of the hydromorphological state of rivers can still be made.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Satellite Insights into methane Super-Emitters: Regional emissions and yearly growth on Turkmenistan’s west coast
abstract: • First report of Turkmen methane super-emitters using China’s GF-5B, ZY-1E, and ZY-1F. • Methane emissions rose ∼ 7 % yearly (2020–2023), corresponding to gas production growth. • Hyperspectral satellite data matches Sentinel-2/Landsat trend estimates. Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from super-emitters on Turkmenistan make it a major global methane hotspot, yet regional emissions and temporal dynamics of these super-emitter sources remain poorly characterized. This study presents a joint analysis of CH 4 point source emissions along Turkmenistan’s west coast using multi-satellite hyperspectral observations from PRISMA and Advanced Hyperspectral Imagers (AHSIs) onboard Chinese satellites GF-5B, ZY-1E, and ZY-1F during 2020–2024. We identified 38 point sources with 256 plumes across 1078 satellite overpasses, revealing total regional intermittent emissions of 0.60 (+0.39/-0.29) Tg·a –1 . Individual plumes emission rates ranged from 0.37 ± 0.10 to 34.13 ± 11.98 t·h –1 , with 25 of 38 sources associated with inefficient flaring operations. A significant ∼ 7 % annual increase in emissions from 2020 to 2023 corresponds with growth in natural gas production. This estimate of annual increase is consistent with that from multispectral satellites of Sentinel-2 and Landsat. Integration of multi-satellite hyperspectral data enhances detection capabilities, enabling finer plume delineation and improving emission quantification. Our findings show emissions consistent with EDGAR v8.0 inventories but nearly three times that of EDGAR v2024, revealing substantial inventory inconsistencies. These findings underscore the importance of high-resolution satellite monitoring for accurate emission inventories and methane mitigation.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Spatiotemporal crime prediction and fairness-constrained spatial optimization with deep reinforcement learning for patrol region design
abstract: • Presents a unified framework for spatio-temporal crime prediction and patrol allocation. • Proposes MRD-MCLP, a patrol location model balancing coverage and fairness. • Develops a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to efficiently solve MRD-MCLP. Existing police resource allocation relies on the prediction of historical crime hotspots, which is difficult to balance the overall effectiveness and regional fairness, resulting in an imbalance in the allocation of resources and difficulty in adapting to dynamic security needs. Taking Los Angeles as the study area, this study first constructs an XGBoost regression prediction model to quantify the future crime risk of each area based on the crime location and time information in the historical crime data, and then introduces the minimum regional disparity (MRD) constraint on the basis of which the fairness indicator is integrated into the optimization framework of patrol region allocation. Meanwhile, this study innovatively introduces a deep reinforcement learning method to improve the model’s solution efficiency and adaptability under complex constraints by interacting with the environment through a policy network. The experimental results show that the MRD fairness model significantly improves resource allocation fairness. Compared with the maximum coverage model, the Gini coefficient and coefficient of variation decrease by 42.56 % and 57.59 %, respectively, and the Jain’s fairness index simultaneously increases by 94.33 %. Regarding patrol region configuration, the proposed method decreases resource redundancy by 66.62 % and increases the spatial balance of facility distribution by 7.5 %, thereby effectively improving resource utilization and spatial layout rationality. Additionally, the deep reinforcement learning (DRL) strategy substantially reduces computational time compared to the classical mixed-integer programming solver, efficiently meeting dual constraints of fairness and coverage effectiveness. In summary, this study integrates MRD constraints and DRL to achieve equitable, efficient policing resource allocation, providing a practical and effective technical pathway for addressing fairness and efficiency demands.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A transformer-based landform mapping method combining topographic knowledge and digital elevation data
abstract: • We propose a topographic knowledge-integrated transformer for landform mapping. • Terrain feature-guided attention enhance feature encoding of landform structures. • A topographic prior loss is proposed to constrain the learning process. • Efficient decoder design supports multi-scale fusion with lower computation. • Outperforms seven baseline models in both qualitative and quantitative assessments. Deep learning (DL) methods have emerged as potential tools for automated landform mapping. However, current approaches frequently overlook critical topographic features and prior topographic knowledge, which are essential for accurate landform differentiation. Consequently, these approaches struggle to resolve indistinct class boundaries and misclassification in transitional landform zones. The application of transformer-based approaches to landform mapping remains rare, although these methods are well-suited for capturing global geomorphic patterns. In this study, we develop TKGFormer, a topographic knowledge-guided and transformer-based DL model specifically designed for landform classification. This model explicitly integrates terrain residuals and multi-scale terrain feature-guided attention mechanisms to emphasise key topographic features and improve classification accuracy. We introduce a topographic feature prior loss function, which constrains the learning process by enforcing consistency between predicted landform classes and fundamental terrain characteristics. Moreover, we design an efficient decoder to enhance multiscale feature fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that TKGFormer outperforms five CNN-based models and two transformer-based model in landform mapping by using bare Earth 30 m resolution Copernicus digital elevation data. In terms of mIoU, TKGFormer exhibits an improvement that ranges from 4.4 % to 20.7 % over the other models. The integration of topographic knowledge into DL provides a promising direction for improving the interpretability and reliability of automated landform classification.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Editorial Board
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: IntDT: A comprehensive roadside dual-lidar dataset and benchmarks for urban intersection digital twins
abstract: The development of digital twins for urban road intersections has attracted significant attention in recent research, driven by their potential to enable intelligent intersections that require accurate and real-time monitoring of dynamic environments. Lidar sensors, with their precise 3D perception capabilities, are particularly well-suited for enhancing intersection perception, offering accurate detection and tracking of road objects, as well as precise velocity estimation. However, existing roadside lidar datasets are deficient in terms of scene diversity and annotation information specifically tailored for intersection monitoring applications. To address the gap, we introduce IntDT, a comprehensive roadside lidar dataset designed specifically for digital twins of intersections. Collected using dual roadside lidar systems across diverse urban intersections, IntDT provides comprehensive annotations that support a range of tasks. Benchmark evaluations are performed for 3D object detection and tracking tasks to facilitate standardized comparative analysis. Additionally, semi-supervised object detection and moving object segmentation are firstly benchmarked for roadside lidar data to stimulate more studies in this field. The dataset will be released at IntDT.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An optical satellite Self-Geolocation method based on Multi-Angle observations
abstract: • Observing an area from different observe angles to realize self-geolocation. • The method is completely independent of calibration fields and easy to implement. • The accuracy calculation formula was derived and validated using simulation data. • Real data experiments proved the accuracy is close to the traditional method. • The execution cost of the algorithm is much lower than traditional algorithms. Traditional optical satellite geometric positioning methods have certain limitations, including the high costs of calibration field construction, the time required, and significant susceptibility to weather conditions at calibration sites. In the present era of ever-increasing satellite constellation deployments, such conventional methods struggle to meet operational demands. Consequently, self-geolocation technologies are receiving more attention. This paper presents a self-geolocation method that completely eliminates the dependency on ground control points. The method uses images acquired during different orbits as inputs and leverages the geographic positioning consistency of corresponding points to calculate a sensor installation matrix without any need for control points. Initial experiments using simulated data revealed the method to be feasible. Subsequent validation using real data from the Luojia 3–02 satellite showed that the positioning accuracy was comparable to traditional method, but the calculation cost was significantly lower. The method will find applications in satellite constellations and long-term precision maintenance missions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Uncertainty aware slum mapping in 55 heterogeneous cities
abstract: Slums are densely populated urban areas characterized by substandard housing and squalor. These areas often lack basic infrastructure and services, making them challenging to manage and improve. Mapping slums on a large scale is particularly difficult due to their complex, dynamic, and non-uniform nature and the scarcity of available data. This study employs deep learning and uncertainty estimation to map slum areas in 55 diverse cities. We tackle the issues of scarce labels, noisy labels, and class imbalance to produce reliable slum probability maps. Applied to a large dataset from the Global South, our method approximates probability values to each image, yielding a more granular view of slum morphology within each city. We achieve this by combining Monte Carlo sampling through test-time augmentation, test-time dropout on overlapping image tiles, and an ensemble of four CNNs. The resulting probability maps not only quantify prediction uncertainty but also reveal morphological patterns of slum settlements. Our findings underscore the diversity and complexity of slums, contributing to a more complete understanding of these environments. A key result is our large-scale workflow, which, despite limited data, groups predictions by probability into multiple slum categories defined by their morphological traits. This approach offers a substantial improvement over traditional binary slum classification methods that focus solely on typical slum morphologies. • Using deep learning to map slums in 55 cities with limited data. • Uncertainty approximation using test-time augmentations, dropout and model ensembles. • Large scale slum dataset: First to use coherent methods and probability estimates for slum mapping. • Maps reveal different slum morphologies, offering crucial insights for urban planning.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Transfer learning for improved crop yield predictions in a cross-scale pathway: a case study for Brazilian national soybean
abstract: Crop yield prediction at a fine spatial scale is crucial for improving agricultural management and resource allocations. Many countries and regions lack fine-scale yield data for fine-scale modeling and thus have to use a “cross-scale pathway”, where coarse-scale (e.g., state-level) data are used to train a model for fine-scale (e.g., county-level or field-level) yield predictions. However, the cross-scale pathway has limited effectiveness in predicting yield due to issues with data availability and model scalability. In this study, we quantify the benefits of transfer learning in the cross-scale pathway. We applied transfer learning by fine-tuning a previously trained and validated AI-based machine learning model, originally developed for field-level soybean yield predictions in the United States, using Brazilian state-level data to predict Brazilian municipal-level soybean yield. Despite differences in environmental conditions, crop phenology, and yield responses between the U.S. and Brazil, we show that transfer learning improves the municipal-level predictions from the cross-scale pathway by increasing the R 2 from 0.29 (without transfer learning) to 0.44. Notably, this is achieved without using any municipal-level data and relying only on scarce state-level observations. When the municipal-level data were used, the transfer learning achieved an R 2 of 0.57, the most stable high performance compared with previous studies. The effectiveness of the cross-scale pathway, thus, increases from 50% to 78% with transfer learning. These findings demonstrate the benefits of transfer learning in the cross-scale pathway under data-limited conditions, and underscore the potential for global crop yield predictions across scales.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: EEMD disentangles climate-NPP dynamics in Southwest China’s karst area: Soil moisture overtakes precipitation as a key driver of afforestation-induced carbon sinks
abstract: • Extract interannual variation components of nonlinear time series data using EEMD. • Post-2001 reforested areas exhibit higher carbon sink potential. • After 2001, SMsurf was the most important limiting factor for forest NPP. • Ecological engineering afforestation projects positively impact forest carbon sinks. The vegetation greening trend resulting from afforestation in the Southwest China’s karst (SCK) area has attracted significant research attention. Identifying the interannual variation in net primary productivity (NPP), its sustained reaction to climate change, and differences between new and old forests before and after afforestation is vital in assessing the effect of the climate on the carbon sink potential of ecosystems. Using monthly NPP and climate data for 1981–2019, ensemble empirical mode decomposition was employed for the extraction of the interannual signal, and new and old forests were compared based on changepoint detection and forest-age data. According to the results, (1) NPP change significantly increased in 1981–2019; after 2001, the NPP growth rate in new forests was 1.47 times that in the old forests, indicating greater carbon sink potential. (2) NPP was sensitive to climate change on an interannual scale, and the sensitivity increased further after 2001. (3) Additionally, the main determinant of NPP in old and new forests shifted from precipitation to soil surface water content after 2001,which closely aligns with the implementation of large-scale ecological restoration projects. The findings reveal that afforestation reinforces water constraints and shifts the dominant climatic control, providing a basis for evaluation of ecological restoration effectiveness in the SCK area and supporting incorporation of water and carbon trade-offs into afforestation planning and routine forest management. This study also provides methodological and case-based support for conducting climate sensitivity assessments of afforestation initiatives across different countries and regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Fine-tuned deep models for niche datasets — People detection in UAV building images to aid rescue operations
abstract: Flood victims are often trapped inside buildings or stranded on rooftops, making their detection a critical aspect of effective rescue operations. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as an essential tool for disaster response, particularly in locating stranded individuals during flooding events. However, existing datasets do not specifically cater to this application, limiting the effectiveness of state-of-the-art (SOTA) object detection models in such scenarios. To bridge this gap, a novel public dataset called the NITC person rescue dataset is introduced. It consists of UAV-captured images of individuals stranded within buildings and on rooftops with two types of labels: bounding boxes and image captions. This dataset presents challenging environmental conditions that significantly impact the performance of pre-trained models. In particular, these models struggle with detecting individuals behind windows, highlighting the limitations of applying general-purpose object detection models to domain-specific tasks. This performance deterioration emphasizes the need for fine-tuning to adapt these models to specialized rescue scenarios. This work systematically evaluates various fine-tuning strategies and their effectiveness in improving model performance. The advantages of model-structure-based fine-tuning are illustrated using YOLOv9 and YOLOv11 as case studies. The best-performing model achieves an AP@50 of 87% for detecting person instances on unseen data. State-of-the-art vision language models (VLMs), BLIP2 and Qwen2-VL are fine-tuned using ground-truth image captions to obtain meaningful descriptions of the seen.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: BF-CNet: A Bayesian-informed probabilistic fusion network to address cloud-induced data gaps in ocean remote sensing
abstract: A B S T R A C TOcean remote sensing provides essential data for diverse marine applications, yet its effectiveness is often compromised by cloud cover. Consequently, removing cloud interference is a fundamental preprocessing stage in ocean remote sensing. Most current cloud removal methods rely on deterministic deep learning models. Despite demonstrating efficacy in cloud removal, these models exhibit inherent limitations, notably their inability to quantify the uncertainty associated with reconstructed cloud regions and their inability to evaluate the cloud-induced uncertainty propagating to downstream applications. To address this limitation, we introduce Bayesian Field Convolutional Neural Networks, a novel probabilistic deep learning model featuring an uncertainty feature extraction module based on Bayesian Neural Fields, while also deeply integrating with the spatiotemporal prediction capabilities of ConvLSTM. This fusion enhances model's spatiotemporal inference capability, allowing it to infer data evolution in novel spatial contexts (regions obscured by clouds) and over extended temporal horizons (the next seven days), and crucially, to quantify the uncertainty of the inferred results. We systematically designed and optimized each individual module, subsequently comparing the 50th percentile output from resulting BF-CNet model against Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks on the cloud-covered dataset. Experiments show that BF-CNet, while successfully quantifying inference uncertainty, achieves a 49.9% improvement in cloud removal accuracy and reduces model running time by 45.9%. Moreover, BF-CNet demonstrates significant robustness under increasing cloud coverage. Our research demonstrates the great potential of probabilistic deep learning models for addressing the challenges inherent in spatiotemporal inference using cloud-obscured sequences, delivering compelling performance and providing valuable technical support for future applications in ocean remote sensing.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Europe’s Double Threat: Evolving patterns of compound heatwaves and droughts
abstract: • Compound hot and dry events (CHDEs) have intensified across Europe since 1980. • Mediterranean regions, especially southern and southeastern Europe, show the strongest trends. • High-severity hotspots are found in Spain, Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Bulgaria. • Extreme CHDEs have become more frequent and longer lasting in recent decades. • Urgent, region-specific adaptation is needed in vulnerable areas. Compound Hot and Dry Events (CHDEs), the co-occurrence of heatwaves (HWs) and dry events (DEs), are intensifying across Europe, heightening risks to human health, agriculture, and ecosystems. This study quantifies the spatiotemporal evolution, frequency, duration, and severity of CHDEs from 1980 to 2023 and identifies both persistent hotspots and emerging risk regions. A compound-event detection framework combining percentile-based HW thresholds (85th, 90th, 95th) with Effective Drought Index (EDI) metrics was applied to E-OBS daily data at 0.1° resolution for the warm season (May–September). Three indicators, frequency, total occurrence, and severity, were used to assess long-term trends and spatial variability. Vector analysis decomposed CHDE drivers, estimating the relative contributions of HWs and DEs. Results show a 35–45% increase in annual CHDEs after 2000, with severe 7-day events (95th percentile) rising by 2.7% per year. The Mediterranean basin (Iberia, southern France, Italy, Greece, western Turkey) remains the principal hotspot, while central and northern Europe (Germany, Poland, the Baltic region, southern Scandinavia) have experienced a three- to five-fold rise in frequency. Vector angles (mean ≈12°) and magnitudes indicate HWs as the dominant driver, with DEs amplifying risks regionally. Urban areas exhibit 60–70% higher growth rates than rural zones, reflecting strong Urban Heat Island effects. These findings highlight two adaptation priorities: (1) enhancing drought–heat resilience in the Mediterranean (MED)through water-efficient agriculture and heat-health preparedness, and (2) strengthening monitoring and early-warning systems in emerging northern hotspots. The study underscores the urgent need for compound-aware, region-specific strategies to safeguard Europe’s food, water, and energy security under future warming scenarios.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Flower color index for detecting and monitoring warm-colored flowering across scales
abstract: • The novel flower color index (FCI) can detect flowering events. • FCI is simple and fast to assess abundance, distribution, and dynamics of flowering. • Robust to different environments, scales, and geographic locations. • Applicable to any optical remote sensing data that has RGB-NIR. Flowers provide significant ecological and economic benefits. Despite rapid technological progress and broad availability of remote sensing data, flower detection and monitoring are still challenging because many phenological studies rely on vegetation indices (e.g., normalized difference vegetation index, NDVI) which are not well-suited for flowers. Although some studies have focused on detection of flowering, the development and application of a comprehensive and robust remote sensing method for flowering remains largely unexplored. In this study, we introduce the flower color index (FCI) for detecting four major warm flower colors—red, pink, purple, and yellow—by leveraging remote sensing bands including blue (B), green (G), red (R) and near-infrared (NIR); these bands are widely available across a variety of remote sensing platforms.
