Here, we demonstrate the application of FCI across species representing a range of vegetation forms (herbaceous, shrubs, and trees) and study locations, corresponding to global biodiversity hotspots. We also tested FCI performance utilizing imagery with different spatial resolution—SkySat (0.5 m), PlanetScope (3 m), and Landsat (30 m). We show that FCI effectively detects and quantifies flowering events, which can be widely applied in ecology (e.g., flowering phenology, species identification, biodiversity conservation), agriculture (e.g., pollination management, yield estimation), and ecotourism (e.g., cherry blossom festival). Our proposed FCI has a simple formulation, is fast to calculate, and robust to different environments (urban or natural), spatial scales (spatial resolution and spatial extent), and background effects. Optimal FCI threshold—though variable across environments and settings—consistently lies on the right side of the distribution, facilitating automatic flower detection.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An approach to detect and map forest canopy layers in Swiss mountain forests using nationwide airborne laser scanning data
abstract: Understanding vertical forest structure is essential for forest management and is strongly linked to ecosystem functioning. In countries with protective forests, sustainable management is key to protecting humans and infrastructure from natural hazards. Well-structured forests usually feature multiple canopy layers, enhancing resistance and resilience to natural disturbances, reducing vulnerability to natural hazards, and improving adaptation to environmental changes. Forests with a single canopy layer often require prioritised and targeted management to increase their structural complexity. Hence, mapping forest canopy layering is crucial for effective forest management and risk mitigation. We developed a reproducible method for large-scale mapping of forest canopy layering to support sustainable forest management. Using airborne laser scanning data, we combined tree- and area-based methods to distinguish between single- and multi-layered forest areas in Switzerland. Our study encompasses four forest ecoregions, seven altitudinal vegetation belts, and a variety of topographic and climatic conditions. The resulting canopy layering map (resolution 10 x 10 m) was validated against two forest structure data sets, one from the Swiss National Forest Inventory (279 plots) and an Independent Forester Assessment (198 plots), yielding overall accuracies of 68 % and 81 %, respectively. Our study provides a robust and scalable method for mapping forest canopy layering across large mountain areas, which is transferable to other regions. Validation across various environmental settings demonstrates the suitability of the approach for nationwide use. Our forest canopy layering map supports sustainable, climate change-adapted forest management decisions, helping to set management priorities that promote well-structured forests for the future.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Pavement crack segmentation with deep orthogonal-enhanced generative model
abstract: As high-resolution road-surface imagery provides a dynamic digital twin of pavement conditions, accurate crack segmentation serves as a key step in constructing intelligent maintenance systems. However, most existing segmentation models assume uniform sampling conditions and rely on fixed parameters, limiting their generalization under diverse real-world environments. To address this challenge, we propose a Deep Orthogonal-Enhanced Generative Model (DORGM) for robust pavement crack segmentation. The proposed framework introduces two key innovations: (1) an orthogonal constraint module that enforces feature disentanglement in the latent space, separating condition-specific noise from intrinsic crack patterns to reduce interference; and (2) a soft-label routing mechanism that adaptively assigns samples to specialized pathways, capturing subtle distributional shifts through Bayesian clustering within a variational framework. These modules can be seamlessly integrated into existing segmentation architectures, improving adaptability without additional retraining. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets including DeepCrack, CRACK500, CFD, and NHA12D show consistent improvements — approximately 5% increase in mIoU and mDice — over baselines such as PSPNet, DNLNet, PointRend, SegFormer, and VPD. By enforcing orthogonality in the latent space, DORGM effectively disentangles environmental variations (e.g., lighting or weather-induced noise) from core crack features, yielding stable and interpretable segmentation across heterogeneous data sources. This disentanglement further mitigates domain shifts that hinder digital twin applications, enabling more reliable integration of crack data with other urban layers such as traffic flow and structural health metrics. • We propose a novel deep generative model to enhance pavement crack segmentation. • an orthogonal constraint module is introduced to enforce orthogonality of features. • a soft-label-based routing mechanism is designed to differentiate sampling variations. • The proposed deep generative model boosts segmentation accuracy in deep learning.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Radar-optical fusion of Sentinel-1/2 for high-resolution NDVI reconstruction and landscape-driven carbon flux assessment in Kuala Selangor, Malaysia (2020–2024)
abstract: • CRFNet radar–optical fusion reconstructs seamless 10 m NDVI in cloudy tropics. • Method restores NDVI continuity across diverse land covers for landscape analysis. • NDVI drives land-cover-specific LUE and Rh models to map monthly NEP at 10 m. • Landscape metrics reveal fragmentation-driven carbon-source hotspots in NEP. • Workflow is transferable for fine-scale carbon monitoring in tropical regions. Reliable quantification of carbon fluxes in humid tropical regions is constrained by persistent cloud cover, heterogeneous land mosaics, and the limited resolution of existing products. To address these challenges, this study developed a Cloud-Resilient Fusion Network (CRFNet) that integrates Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter with cloud-screened Sentinel-2 NDVI using a CNN–BiLSTM–multi-head attention architecture. The framework reconstructed 10 m NDVI time series in Kuala Selangor, Malaysia (2020–2024), achieving annual R 2 above 0.82 and RMSE below 0.12, thereby improving temporal continuity under heavy cloud–rainfall interference. The reconstructed NDVI was used to drive a light-use-efficiency model for net ecosystem productivity (NEP) estimation, supported by temperature-based heterotrophic respiration. Results showed a 7.4 % decline in mean annual NEP across five years, with degraded mangroves and sloping croplands emerging as hotspots of sink-to-source transitions. Landscape analysis revealed strong structure–function coupling: stable forests and mangroves were characterized by large cohesive patches with largest patch index values above 40 % and edge density below 20 m ha -1 , while croplands and degraded slopes exhibited higher patch numbers, reduced patch dominance, and greater edge complexity, which increased carbon source risk. By linking fine-scale NDVI reconstruction with process-based carbon modeling and landscape metrics, this study provides a transferable workflow for high-resolution carbon flux monitoring and a robust scientific basis for carbon budget assessment, ecosystem management, and carbon-neutrality planning in tropical monsoon regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: On the use of SWOT altimetry data for monitoring coastal hydrodynamics
abstract: Nowadays, most of satellite altimeters has proven to provide an effective dataset of sea surface changes in oceans and continental-shelf toward nearshore zones. The need to extend the satellite use to sea level and wave monitoring closest to the coast has introduced in several works to investigate the accuracy of observations at shallow water areas and coastal zones. This work has been conducted in the framework of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath interferometric altimetry mission. Here, we provide insights into SWOT’s ability to monitor the nearshore and coastal Sea Surface Heights (SSH) and Significant Wave Height (SWH) in the English Channel, along the United Kingdom and French coasts with a special focus on high energetic periods, including storms. SWOT observations, including the 1-day Cal/Val and Scientific Orbit data, have been used to assess their performance, compared to in-situ measurements. This finding has exhibited good agreements between SWOT altimetry and in-situ measurements for both SSH and SWH with a maximum STD of 85 cm. A benchmarking analysis of SWOT observations for assessing coastal waves has shown significant results within a ~3-4 km radius and ~ 8-12 m depth from the coastline. This work presents the first investigation of the SWOT contribution for monitoring coastal hydrodynamics at shallow water areas. This challenging issue will benefit from SWOT ongoing works to offer reliable estimates of coastal hydrodynamics, which is crucial for improving numerical models at both regional and local scales.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Monitoring soil substrate influence in vineyards using Sentinel-2 time series and land surface phenology
abstract: • The effect of soil substrate on vineyard responses over time was investigated using optical satellite imagery. • Land Surface Phenology was assessed to determine which method and vegetation index provided the most stable results across years. • A Random Forest model with a nested resampling validation technique was used to classify vineyard responses. • A novel approach for detecting soil substrate effects on vineyards over time was proposed. This work explores the potential of Sentinel-2 time-series imagery to investigate the differences in vineyards associated with varying soil substrates. The investigation was carried out by selecting vineyards in the Piana Rotaliana wine growing area of the autonomous province of Trento (Italy). Consistent time-series datasets were defined by selecting vineyards trained under the same trellis system and avoiding plantation renewal between 2017 and 2023. To extract Land Surface Phenology (LSP) the best configuration between vegetation indices and fitting methods for deriving LSP features was investigated. The results indicate that Enhanced Vegetation Index 2 (EVI2) provides better stability with respect to Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). For each vineyard statistical metrics were derived like LSP, Growing Season (GS; good observation within the LSP time period) and off Season (good observation outside the LSP time period) metrics. Eight datasets were defined and a Random Forest model was employed to assess classification accuracy and evaluate its stability across the years. Findings suggest that the substrate effect can be distinguished both from off Season and Growing Season metrics. Vegetation water content indices, such as the Global Vegetation Moisture Index (GVMI), emerged as the most effective and temporally stable predictors. The off Season datasets provided generally better results with respect to GS datasets when the model of one year was tested over the remaining years. The results provide valuable insights into the potential influence of soil characteristics on grapevine response over time, by highlighting the water retention capacity of the substrate and the vineyard response.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Phenology-adapted potato mapping index (PMI) for ground sample-free identification
abstract: Potato is the world's most important non-cereal food crop, crucial for global food security and agricultural sustainability. Large-scale potato mapping faces persistent challenges, primarily due to scarce training samples, complex background crop compositions, and limited spectral distinctiveness compared to staple crops. To overcome the persistent limitations in ground data dependency, we propose a novel Potato Mapping Index (PMI) that leverages Sentinel-2 temporal phenology to enable scalable potato identification without field sampling. The PMI operates dynamically based on crop phenological stages, utilizing Sentinel-2 bands (B8 (NIR) and B12 (SWIR-2)) and indices (normalized difference built-up index (NDBI) and red edge normalized difference vegetation index (RENDVI)) to accentuate spectral differences between potatoes and background crops. This approach effectively isolates the unique spectral signature of potato crops, facilitating accurate and efficient mapping. Validated across multiple years and in six key potato-producing countries (Belgium, China, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, and the United States), the PMI achieved an average overall accuracy (OA) of 91.75% and Kappa coefficients exceeding 0.8. These performance metrics are notably higher than those of the traditional supervised classifier, random forest (RF) model, which yielded an average OA of 90.0% and an average Kappa coefficient of 0.72. The resulting maps show high agreement with reference datasets, demonstrating robust spatiotemporal generalization. These findings offer a novel and valuable approach for global-scale potato mapping.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multimodal cross fusion Mamba network for remote sensing image semantic segmentation with complementary masked self-supervision
abstract: Deep learning-based multimodal remote sensing image (RSI) semantic segmentation models have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to leverage complementary information across modalities, resulting in more robust and accurate Earth observation. However, most existing approaches rely predominantly on convolutional neural networks with limited receptive fields or transformer-based architectures that are computationally intensive. In this study, we proposed a multimodal cross fusion Mamba (MCF-Mamba) network for multimodal RSI semantic segmentation, aiming to collaboratively enhance accuracy and efficiency. The proposed network features three core components: a dual-branch VMamba encoder, a multimodal cross-Mamba fusion module, and a U-shaped Mamba decoder. The architecture with a unified structure centered on the selective state space model ensures that it achieves global perception with linear complexity. Furthermore, for addressing the constraint of limited labeled samples in practical applications, we developed a generative multimodal complementary masked self-supervised (CMSS) strategy. It leverages abundant unlabeled RSIs to learn generalized multimodal representations by modeling intermodal complementary consistency. Extensive experiments on three public datasets involving optical-SAR and optical-DEM modalities demonstrated that the proposed network and strategy are superior to other advanced segmentation models and self-supervised methods in land cover mapping and building extraction tasks. The MCF-Mamba network achieves the highest accuracy while significantly reducing both model size and computational cost, and further improves the accuracy and generalization through the CMSS strategy. The source code is available at https://github.com/Xiao-RS/MCFMamba_CMSS .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: An improved Alpha approximation algorithm for time-series surface soil moisture inversion from Sentinel-1 SAR data
abstract: • The optimization of constraint strategy is achieved using a “dynamic constraint” • The underdetermination problem is revised by adding effective information. • The retrieval precision of the improved Alpha approximation algorithm is validated. • An improved algorithm for soil moisture inversion from microwave data is presented. Accurate measurement of soil moisture content has significant scientific value and social benefits for studying global or regional water cycle mechanisms, developing climate and hydrological models, and advancing sustainable agricultural development. The Alpha approximation algorithm is regarded as one of the primary representatives among change detection methods and has been widely applied in soil moisture inversion. However, as the inversion time extends, the accumulation and propagation of inversion errors lead to a decrease in the inversion accuracy of the alpha approximation algorithm. In this study, three soil moisture observation networks, Tianjun, Nagqu, and Daman, in northwestern China are used as the research region. The optimization of the constraint strategy of the Alpha approximation algorithm is conducted by combining the Dubois model and Juxtaposition approach. The underdetermination issue of the Alpha approximation algorithm is also resolved by incorporating multi-angle synchronous observations to enrich the number of effective equations. Finally, we obtain an improved Alpha approximation algorithm based on the above approaches, and its inversion accuracy is also validated in the three study areas. Compared to the original alpha approximation algorithm, the improved algorithm demonstrates a significant enhancement in inversion accuracy. The RMSE, Bias, and R 2 of the retrieval results in Tianjun region are 0.074 cm 3 /cm 3 , 0.452, and 0.682, respectively. Furthermore, the improved Alpha approximation algorithm also shows satisfactory performance across different regions and land surfaces. The RMSE, Bias, and R 2 of the retrieval results in Nagqu observation networks are 0.076 cm 3 /cm 3 , 0.437, and 0.732 respectively. The RMSE, Bias, and R 2 of the retrieval results in Daman observation networks are 0.05 cm 3 /cm 3 , 0.269, and 0.533, respectively. Meanwhile, the freezing and thawing processes, vegetation changes, and agriculture practices are the major considerations influencing the inversion accuracy of the Alpha approximation algorithm.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A comparative study of deep learning methods for super-resolution of NPP-VIIRS nighttime light images
abstract: Nighttime light imagery plays a crucial role in diverse applications such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, and economic analysis. Although NPP-VIIRS provides a long and continuous Nighttime light time series, its relatively low spatial resolution limits detailed spatial analysis. Achieving Nighttime light data with both high spatial and temporal resolution remains a key challenge. This study investigates the effectiveness of several deep learning–based super-resolution (SR) models for enhancing NPP-VIIRS Nighttime light imagery using Luojia1-01 data as high-resolution reference imagery. Five representative models—ESPCN, RDN, SRFBN, SwinIR, and RealESRGAN—were selected to cover a range of network architectures including CNN, RNN, ResNet, DenseNet, Transformer, and GAN. A paired SR dataset was constructed from Luojia1-01 and NPP-VIIRS images, and the selected models were trained and evaluated on this dataset. Model performance was assessed across different urban scales and lighting conditions (e.g., dense urban cores, road networks) using PSNR, SSIM, FSIM, and the 95th percentile metrics. Results indicate that model performance varies substantially across scene types, with RealESRGAN showing superior detail recovery and overall image quality (PSNR = 31.96, SSIM = 0.85, FSIM = 0.85). The 95th percentile distribution of the RealESRGAN-enhanced images closely matches that of high-resolution reference data. These findings demonstrate that deep learning–based SR methods can substantially improve the spatial resolution and visual quality of NPP-VIIRS Nighttime light imagery, enabling finer-scale analysis of urban structures and temporal dynamics. This work provides an effective technical framework for reconstructing historical high-resolution Nighttime light data and expanding their applicability in urban, environmental, and socioeconomic studies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mapping mangrove forest degradation using lidar and Landsat data
abstract: • This paper proposes a novel approach for mapping mangrove forest degradation. • Degradation indicators were selected from mangrove forest structure and function. • Development of a new method to establish a spatial–temporal reference frame. • Improvement of hierarchical models to estimate large-area mangrove biomass. • The overall mangrove degradation in 2022 on Hainan Island was 30.78%. Monitoring mangrove forest degradation is challenging compared to deforestation because degradation involves the loss of ecosystem structure and function without changing forest cover, and selecting appropriate degradation references is difficult. Existing remote sensing time-series approaches offer a practical way to monitor forest degradation, but they mainly monitor degradation that occurred after images became available and focus on the forest’s horizontal dimension. This study proposes a novel approach for quantifying mangrove forest degradation. The approach evaluates the degree of mangrove degradation by comparing degradation indicators (canopy cover, canopy height, and aboveground biomass) with benchmark values inside environmentally homogeneous land capacity sub-regions. The benchmark values are determined by combining the LandTrendr algorithm and land capacity knowledge, accounting for temporal and spatial reference types. Large-area mangrove degradation indicators were estimated using improved hierarchical models with a “feed-forward” strategy. We applied this approach to mangrove forests on Hainan Island, China. The results showed that the overall accuracy of degradation identification was 95%, with a kappa coefficient of 0.90. The overall mangrove degradation degree in 2022 was 30.78% on Hainan Island, with reductions of 38.01% in canopy height, 28.04% in canopy cover, and 26.27% in aboveground biomass, indicating that mangrove dwarfing was the most serious degradation issue. Protected areas exhibited lower degradation (29.89%) than unprotected areas (35.31%). The findings also showed that the approach successfully detected degradation signals earlier than those from traditional satellite remote sensing data could to a certain extent (e.g., Landsat imagery dating back to ∼1985). The R 2 values (RMSE) for the canopy height, canopy cover, and biomass models were 0.72 (1.03 m), 0.85 (0.11), and 0.69 (43.99 Mg/ha), respectively. The proposed approach can be an alternative to time series-based methods when mangrove degradation has a long-term history and can provide critical information to support mangrove conservation and restoration efforts.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SOUL: A weakly supervised framework for Martian rock segmentation using scribble labels
abstract: Accurate semantic information about Martian rocks from rover images is crucial for scientific investigation and safe rover navigation. Due to the high cost and difficulty of obtaining dense manual annotations in Martian rock imagery, existing studies have focused mostly on semi-supervised and transfer learning strategies. However, segmentation under extremely sparse annotation conditions has not yet been investigated sufficiently. To fill this gap, we proposed a weakly supervised learning (WSL) framework, namely, Scribble-guided Object Uncertainty-aware Learning (SOUL), for Martian rock segmentation using scribble annotations. SOUL comprises two key components: an Object-level Pseudo-label Generation (OPG) strategy to generate pseudo-labels with accurate boundary characterization and an Uncertainty-aware Prototype-guided (UAPG) loss to refine the noisy pseudo-labels. Specifically, OPG generates object-level pseudo-labels by integrating instance decomposition with the Segment Anything Model (SAM), scribble-guided label assignment, and similarity-based label propagation. UAPG estimates pixel-wise uncertainty via modeling prototype-based feature similarities, enabling confidence-aware optimization. Extensive experiments on the TWMARS, MarsData-V2, and MSLRock datasets demonstrated that SOUL effectively increased segmentation quality under sparse supervision, outperforming six recent benchmarks. Moreover, ablation studies illustrated that both OPG and UAPG are crucial for enhancing segmentation performance. Furthermore, SOUL narrows the gap between weak and semi-supervision and between weak and full supervision. Overall, SOUL has great potential to reduce manual annotation effort while retaining competitive accuracy. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/Tong-777777/SOUL .
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Generating photorealistic urban digital twins with Occlusion-Aware texture mapping
abstract: High resolution textures play a vital role in enhancing realism of urban digital twins, particularly in applications such as urban planning, energy analysis, and geospatial visualization. While textures can provide valuable surface-level details—such as material types (e.g., windows, green façades, bricks) and sunlight reflectance (albedo), these details are often missing in existing 3D city models. Existing 3D city models lack very high-resolution textures, limiting their realism and use cases. Manual texture mapping is labor-intensive and becomes impractical at city scale, often requiring days to weeks of effort. To address this gap, we present the CityJSON Texture Mapper, a Python-based software tool for the automated texture mapping of CityJSON 3D city models from oblique and nadir aerial imagery. The tool assumes that interior and exterior orientation parameters are available, ensuring spatial alignment between the 3D geometry and the images. Our approach introduces a novel image selection algorithm based on ray-tracing visibility analysis and integrates optimization techniques such as occlusion-aware texture mapping, texture atlassing, and optimization methods. Experimental results demonstrate the tool’s effectiveness in producing high-quality, visually enriched 3D models, significantly reducing the time and effort required for manual processing. Proposed optimization methods reduce the number of textures by 97%, the total texture size by 63%, and the CityJSON file size by 37% relative to the non-optimized model. Although this study focused on one urban area, the methodology is scalable to large city datasets and suitable for national-level applications involving thousands of buildings. Visualization of textured model generated using developed method is available at: https://bit.ly/textured3dbag .

title: Global high-resolution mapping of photovoltaic power plants from 2019 to 2025 using unsupervised index-based multi-source data fusion method
abstract: • An efficient framework enables rapid and low-cost global PV plant mapping. • The adaptive index-based data fusion method ensures more accurate PV extraction. • The first 10 m-resolution global PV mapping product from 2019 to 2025. • The mapping product delivers the most up-to-date global PV plant distribution. • Spatio-temporal PV diffusion and land-use changes are systematically revealed. Accurate mapping of photovoltaic (PV) power plants is critical for monitoring the development of solar energy generation and supporting PV operational management, policy-making, and environmental analysis. However, existing geospatial datasets of PV power plants are either limited in spatial coverage, insufficient in resolution and accuracy, or outdated and lack timely updates, thus failing to meet these demands. To address this, we develop an efficient framework for global PV mapping that integrates the proposed adaptive normalized difference photovoltaic index (ANDPI) with a multi-source data fusion algorithm to extract accurate contours of PV power plants from Sentinel-2 imagery. We generate the global mapping product of PV power plants at 10 m resolution from 2019 to 2025. This mapping achieves an overall accuracy of 91.16 %, outperforming existing PV mapping products, while maintaining the processing speed of 140 km 2 per second. Our analysis reveals that the global PV area expanded from 8432 km 2 in 2019 to 16289 km 2 in 2025, with China contributing 61 % of the growth. Besides, PV power plants are primarily deployed on rangeland (44.0 %) and cropland (40.1 %). Cropland held a slight dominance before 2021, after which rangeland accounted for a larger proportion. To the best of our knowledge, this geospatial dataset represents the most comprehensive global PV mapping product, offering the global spatial coverage, the highest resolution, and the most up-to-date information. It provides valuable insights into the spatial distribution and expansion of PV power plants, contributing to global strategies for carbon neutrality and sustainable development. The code and data are available at https://github.com/SUNNYTREE-LAB/Fusion_PV_Mapping.

title: InSAR-based landslide susceptibility analysis in karst erosion landforms using a non-landslide sampling strategy
abstract: • Propose an LSA framework with non-landslide sampling in low InSAR deformation areas. • Conduct LSA in areas with high vegetation coverage and karst erosion landforms. • Apply SHAP algorithm to explain global and local mechanisms in LSA. Landslide Susceptibility Analysis (LSA) is essential for effective geological hazard management, particularly in karst regions where complex terrain and dense vegetation present significant challenges. This study introduces an innovative LSA framework that integrates a low-InSAR deformation sampling strategy (BL-InSAR) to mitigate InSAR errors in surface deformation measurements over densely vegetated areas and reduce uncertainty in non-landslide sample selection. Focusing on Bijie District in Guizhou Province, a karst-dominated region, we incorporate karst hydrogeological data into the LSA process. Utilizing a C-Support Vector Machine (C-SVM) model, we analyze 14 factors, including karst hydrogeology, to generate four landslide susceptibility maps employing BL-InSAR and three conventional sampling methods. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm is applied to elucidate both global and local landslide mechanisms. Our findings identify karst hydrogeology, precipitation, lithology, and slope as key factors influencing landslide susceptibility, with high-risk areas concentrated in the northwest, central, and northeastern regions. The BL-InSAR method achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.8885, outperforming other methods by 2.69 %, 3.66 %, and 8.45 %, respectively. This framework enhances the interpretability of landslide susceptibility models by considering landslide creep dynamics through InSAR and integrating karst hydrogeological data. It offers a more effective approach to capturing and interpreting landslide risks in karst environments, thereby contributing to more reliable LSA in complex terrains.

title: High-resolution local climate zone mapping via deep mixed-scene decomposition of remote sensing imagery
abstract: Under rapid urbanization, traditional single-class LCZ mapping methods fail to represent the coexistence of multiple land-cover types within the same block, resulting in blurred boundaries and reduced accuracy for urban heat-island modeling. To address this, LCZ mapping is reformulated as a mixed-scene unmixing task and tackled with a novel deep-learning framework, MSU-Net. Real street-block morphologies from OpenStreetMap are combined with 1 m Google Earth imagery to create multi-scale inputs that preserve both global block layouts and local detail. MSU-Net comprises a primary unmixing branch reinforced by two auxiliary guidance branches—one driven by purified-image semantic cues, the other by sparse local spatial reconstruction, and a Dual Cross-Attention Fusion (DCAF) module that integrates global–local and global–purified features under non-negativity and sum-to-one constraints. Two block-level datasets covering Wuhan and Shenzhen were created. MSU-Net outperforms existing methods on these datasets, boosting overall accuracy by 15–17 %, reducing mean absolute error by over 35 %, and cutting weighted-difference error by around 30 %. Transfer learning further confirms its robustness across cities with distinct morphologies.
